plannedCharts.title: India climbed from the bottom half of the index to its top third
plannedCharts.unit: % of ranked economies India is ahead of
plannedCharts.subtitle: Share of the other ranked economies that India ranks ahead of, with the 90% interval from the EU Joint Research Centre's audit · GII 2011-2026 · WIPO
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The rank everyone quotes, drawn so that years with different numbers of economies can sit on one line.

plannedCharts.title: India's outputs have outranked its inputs in every edition since 2011
plannedCharts.unit: % of ranked economies India is ahead of
plannedCharts.subtitle: Share of ranked economies India is ahead of, on the input and output sub-indices · GII 2011-2026 · WIPO
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The gap between what goes in and what comes out is older than the climb.

plannedCharts.title: India's 38th could be anywhere from 34th to 39th
plannedCharts.subtitle: GII 2026 rank and its 90% interval, economies ranked 28th to 50th · WIPO, EU Joint Research Centre audit
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: A rank is an estimate; the audit says how firm it is.

plannedCharts.title: India is in the world's top 20 on 15 measures, and below 100th on five
plannedCharts.subtitle: India's rank on each of the 77 GII 2026 indicators with an Indian value, of 139 economies · WIPO
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: One dot per measure shows what the single rank averages over.

plannedCharts.title: Three-quarters of India's lead over a typical economy comes from its outputs
plannedCharts.subtitle: India's 2026 score minus a typical economy's, by pillar, in GII points weighted as the index weights them · median of 139 economies · WIPO
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: It splits India's lead into the parts that make it.

plannedCharts.title: Since 2022, India has risen on both output pillars and slipped on four of five input pillars
plannedCharts.unit: % of ranked economies India is ahead of
plannedCharts.subtitle: Share of ranked economies India is ahead of, by pillar · GII 2022 (132 economies) and 2026 (139) · WIPO
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The recent climb, pillar by pillar.

plannedCharts.title: In the world's top ten by total, far lower per person
plannedCharts.unit: % of economies with data India is ahead of
plannedCharts.subtitle: India's standing among economies with data, by total and per person · latest year since 2018 or 2020 · World Bank WDI (UNESCO, WIPO, NSF, IMF)
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: A country of 1.4 billion looks large on any total; per person is the other half of the truth.

plannedCharts.title: For its income, India scores well above the line
plannedCharts.subtitle: GII 2026 score against GDP per person (PPP dollars, log scale), 139 economies · WIPO, IMF
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Richer countries score higher; the question is how India does for its income.

plannedCharts.title: Five of India's research figures in the index still describe 2020
plannedCharts.subtitle: India's GII 2026 indicators by the year their data describes · WIPO
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: A score is only as current as its inputs.

plannedCharts.title: Even on its new survey, India spends less of its GDP on research than most peers
plannedCharts.subtitle: Gross expenditure on R&D as a share of GDP, latest year since 2018 · UNESCO via World Bank; India's 2023-24 figure from DST
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The input the index cannot see past 2020, checked against India's own newer survey.

plannedCharts.title: India has fewer researchers per person than any peer shown
plannedCharts.subtitle: Full-time-equivalent researchers per million people, latest year since 2014 · UNESCO via World Bank
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: People are the input research money buys.

plannedCharts.title: India's R&D share jumped in 2021-22, the year the survey changed
plannedCharts.subtitle: Gross expenditure on R&D, % of GDP, by fiscal year · DST/NSTMIS R&D Statistics 2022-23 and 2025-26
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: A rise that comes from counting more is not a rise in research.

plannedCharts.title: Universities now file more than half of India's patent applications
plannedCharts.subtitle: Patent applications by Indian applicants, by type of applicant, financial years · IP India annual reports
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: India's patent count is the GII output that rose fastest; who files tells you what it means.

plannedCharts.title: India's share of the world's ICT services exports peaked in 2012
plannedCharts.subtitle: India's computer, communications and other ICT services exports as a share of the world's · 2005-2024 · World Bank (IMF balance of payments)
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: India's first-place indicator, read over twenty years.

plannedCharts.title: India's four clusters are large, but spread over many people
plannedCharts.subtitle: The world's top 100 science and technology clusters: share of world patents, papers and VC deals, against the same per person · GII 2026 · WIPO
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Cities, not countries, are where invention concentrates.

plannedCharts.title: Tamil Nadu files 80 times as many patents per person as Bihar
plannedCharts.subtitle: Patent applications by Indian applicants per million people, by the applicant's state, 2024-25 · IP India; National Commission on Population projections
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The state picture, from India's own patent office.

plannedCharts.title: Among eleven peers, India moved from fourth to third since 2022
plannedCharts.subtitle: Order by GII score among India and ten middle-income peers, 2022 and 2026 · WIPO
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Peers at a similar stage say more than the top of the table.

plannedCharts.title: India leads Viet Nam on knowledge outputs; Viet Nam leads on business sophistication
plannedCharts.subtitle: Share of 139 economies each ranks ahead of, by GII 2026 pillar · WIPO
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The two longest-running overperformers got there by different routes.

selectionRules: Start from the page question, not from the indicator name.
Choose the smallest set of visuals that explains scale, trend, structure, comparison, and caveat.
Prefer mobile-friendly charts: line charts with sparse ticks, horizontal bars, share strips, pyramids only when essential, and no dense tables.
Use one strong pull quote only when the evidence supports it with a number.
Add glossary blocks for technical terms that normal readers may not know.
caveats: Use only figures present in lockedNumbers or sourceSummaries.
If a related theme indicator is present, you may use it for context, but do not pretend it is the main answer.
If source coverage is thin, say so directly.
Do not compare states, districts, or cities unless the evidence packet contains those geographies.
forbiddenClaims: Do not infer causality from a trend unless the evidence explicitly supports it.
Do not cite a source that is not present in sourceSummaries.
